full_judgment:
ATM Afzal CJ : Plaintiff-Appellant's suit for eviction of the defendant-respondent from the suit shop, SCC Suit No. 1 of 1985 of the SCC Court and Second Court, Assistant Judge, Bogra Sadar was decreed but on a revision taken by the defendant, Civil Revision No. 885 of 1986 (Dhaka), a Single Judge of the High Court Division, by the impugned judgment and order dated 26 January 1992, set aside the said decree and now this appeal by leave from the said judgment. 

 5. Although the plaintiff positively stated in his plaint that there was no relationship of landlord and tenant between him and the defendant and the defendant is liable to be evicted without notice as an unauthorised occupant, the learned Assistant Judge surprisingly did not take any issue in that behalf for consideration. The learned Assistant Judge found the defendant to be a defaulter for depositing rent at a time in the House Rent Controller's office. She also found that the suit premises was required by the plaintiff in that the defendant admitted that the plaintiff had purchased the same for bona fide requirement. The learned Assistant Judge also found the defendant to be an unauthorised occupant. In a slip-shod judgment she found that the defendant had not paid rent in spite of his knowledge about the transfer in favour of the plaintiff, that he was a bona fide defaulter and that the disputed premises was required by the plaintiff. The suit was accordingly decreed on 23-9-1986. 

 6. In the revision taken by the defendant against the said decree, the learned Single Judge, who heard the matter, observed that the findings made by the learned SCC Judge as to the defendant being a defaulter and bona fide requirement of the plaintiff was contrary to the plaintiffs own pleading in that he himself stated that there existed no relationship of landlord and tenant between him and the defendant The learned Judge further observed that the learned SCC Judge had herself made out a third case beyond the scope of the pleading and, as such, her judgment was liable to be set aside. The Rule was accordingly made absolute. 

 8. At the hearing of the appeal, Dr. Rafiqur Rahman, learned Advocate for the plaintiff-appellant, submitted that admittedly the plaint was not happily drafted but even then on the defendant's own case he was a defaulter and the plea of bona fide requirement of the plaintiff having been accepted by the trial Court, the decree passed in the suit was quite justified and called for no interference by the High Court Division. 

 9. We shall come to the pleading later on, and, for the present we shall see whether the learned SCC Judge properly made the findings of 'defaulter' and 'bona fide requirement' so as to pass a decree for eviction of the defendant-tenant. In the revision before the High Court Division it was argued on behalf of the defendant that the learned SCC Judge erred in law in making the findings against the defendant in respect of the said two issues. The learned Judge of the High Court Division in view of the plaintiffs own pleading that there was no relationship of landlord and tenant with the defendant observed that the learned SCC Judge had acted contrary to the pleading in determining the said two issues which was thus in excess of her jurisdiction.
